name: C. F. Ellison
role: Ice contractor and agent at Medora; later justice of the peace
bio: Charles F. Ellison, of Dubuque, was foreman of the outfit that put up the company's ice at Medora and built the ice-house at Miles City in early 1884, and by November 1884 he was ice agent for the Northern Pacific Refrigerator Car Company, damming the Little Missouri and laying a track from the dam to the ice houses. In July 1885 the company turned its Medora lumber yard over to him, and that December he finished a house and set up housekeeping with his wife. In 1886 he contracted to put up ice for Bob Roberts and Gill Kennedy, clerked the election that organized school township number 1, and in November was elected a justice of the peace with Howard Eaton. In December 1886 he left for Kansas City to put in order the re-icing stations between there and New York.
